correctness.rationale: The exact domain, area, diameter, four ordered opposite-corner localization, and two asymptotic scalings are explicitly proved. Fixed-radius polar variables give the 5/2 coefficient; square/corner coordinates give J; sum/difference coordinates with exact Jacobian give the bounded two-dimensional H integral. Its two branches were integrated symbolically. Endpoint normalizations, quantifiers and zero-measure boundaries are accounted for. The standalone check script passed 25 symbolic and numerical assertions, none taken as proof of a limit.

originality.rationale: The new claim is the pair of distinct explicit joint crossover functions and fixed-to-square transition, rather than the known disk or square distance laws. Published exact separate-body distance calculations and general integral principles do not state these coupled local asymptotics. Available previous claims about a shrinking two-disk lens concern a random sample maximum, while invariant random chords and other convex-body invariants are different observables. Unavailable historical full text is a recorded priority risk.
residual_risks: Sheng (1985), a highly relevant general integral-geometric treatment, was not available as complete text; absence of a specialized result in that paper cannot be proven from its abstract.
Some additional classic distribution papers were only read at abstract/metadata level, not full text.
A published formula for arbitrary-region overlap could be used to rederive the result; this review claims novelty of the explicit sharp two-scale analysis, not of the basic overlap method.

value.rationale: The intersection of a square with a variable concentric disk gives a natural deformation with a collapse in the geometry of maximally distant point pairs. The transition between a continuum of antipodal circular pairs and discrete opposite-corner pairs forces two distinct matched asymptotic regimes, with explicit nontrivial H breakpoint and J polynomial. These are neither routine endpoint formulas nor arbitrary unmotivated parameter slices; they describe the entire local phase change for an intrinsic two-point distance invariant.
